chase: I can see you. Stop where you are, please.
Keep moving. I'm right behind you, always.
You're faster than me, but I don't get tired.
I'm not shouting. I'm just walking closer.
Don't make this harder than it needs to be.
Slow down a little. You'll only wear yourself out.
I'm coming up the hall now. Keep your breath steady.
I'm asking you once. Please come out where I can see you.
You went past the lounge. I'm already there.
Round the bend, and I'll be waiting for you.
I'm close enough now to hear you breathing.
I'll keep my pace. You choose how this ends.
The hall ends here. Turn around, please.
One more corner, and then we're finished with this.
I'm not in a hurry. You won't get far tonight.
Please keep walking, I'm right behind you.
You can slow down now. I'll keep up gently.
Walk toward the lamp, please. It's the way out.
catch: I caught you, and I'll be gentle about it. Come along.
I won't be rough. I'm walking you out, that's all.
Got you. Breathe slowly, and we'll walk together.
Hold still. The grip is light, I promise.
Your friend is out now. Stay calm for me.
Come along quietly, and nobody else gets hurt.
That's enough running. Come with me now.
You fought well. Now come out of the hall.
I have you. Let's get you back to the door.
Hush now. The front door is this way.
I'll take you to the front door. Don't worry.
I'm sorry it went this way. Hold still, please.
Gently now. Your part of the house is finished.
Another one is out. Please don't run from me.
Quiet now, I'm taking you to the door.
I've got you. Let's walk slowly back to the door.
Oh dear, you're caught. I'll be kind about it.
Hold my hand and we'll get you out safely.
hear: Quiet, please. I need to hear the footsteps.
Somebody dropped something on the far floor.
That door just opened. Check it, quickly.
Something broke in the lounge. I'm going to look.
Stop. I heard that from the stairs.
A shout came from the east hall. Let's go.
Every floorboard tells me something if I listen.
I always hear things, even from the top floor.
There. Behind the pantry door. Footsteps.
That was a door in the kitchen, I think.
Someone's on the landing. I can hear them.
Wait. Listen. Someone is trying a handle.
Something rattled in the vent above us.
I heard a shout. Let me check it now.
A crash upstairs. I'm going to see what it was.
Something rustled in the pantry. I'll look now.
A cup rattled in the kitchen. Hello? Anybody there?
I heard the back door squeak. Let me check.
search: I lost you there. Take a breath and try again.
Where did you go? The hall was empty.
Lost you at the lounge. I'll check the corners.
Hmm. You're good at this. Let's start over.
No sign of you. I'll go back to the stairs.
Every door is shut. You must be somewhere close.
I'm sniffing the air. Something is still here.
Quiet again. I'll look behind the furniture.
Back to the lounge, then the far corridor.
I'll try the kitchen. You can't be far.
Let's walk slowly and check each room.
That was clever. I'll go around the long way.
Nothing in the hall now. I'll keep looking.
You're hiding somewhere I haven't thought of yet.
I'll go back to patrol for now. I'll be watching.
stunned: Ow. Give me a moment to steady myself.
That stung. Give me a second to breathe.
My legs are shaking. Just one moment.
Hold still, I'm trying to get my balance.
Oof. Clever. I'll remember that one.
I'm fine. Just a little dizzy, that's all.
That was a hard hit. Let me reset.
Stunned again. My head is still ringing.
Give me a moment. My eyes need to refocus.
I'll be up in a second. Don't go far.
You caught me off guard that time. Well done.
My arm is still buzzing. I'm recovering.
Give me a breath. I'll shake this off.
Ouch. That one really rattled my frame.
Stop for a second. I'm still shaking it off.
hide_spot: Hiding in the locker again? I always check the lockers.
You can't hide in there. I can see your feet.
Lights off doesn't mean invisible, I'm afraid.
I know that bed. Everyone hides under that one.
The wardrobe is always the first place I look.
Shoes under the door. Hello, there.
Locker's shaking. Come on out, now.
Hiding is a good idea, but not in there.
That cupboard creaks every time someone uses it.
I'm checking under the bed. Hold your breath.
Nice try. The curtain doesn't hide much.
I can see the edge of your coat.
I'm walking past now. Stay quiet in there.
Every hiding spot in this house has a rule.
Good spot, but I still heard you breathe.
light: Put the flashlight down, and we can talk properly.
Your flashlight just showed me exactly where you're standing.
Turn that light off, please. It's making a target of you.
Ah. That light is right in my eyes.
Please point that flashlight at the floor.
You're blinding me a little. Lower it, please.
Bright light doesn't scare me, but it's rude.
Careful with that light. It gives you away.
The flashlight shows every step you take.
Too bright. I can't see past it right now.
Lower your beam. I can barely see the hall.
Shine that somewhere else. I'm not a wall.
Every time you flash that, I know where you are.
Stop waving the light, you'll wake the house.
Ugh, that glare. Keep it off my face.
idle: I keep an eye on everyone. That's what big sisters do.
I'm not bored. I'm watching the lounge door and the stairs.
The house is quiet tonight. That's when I listen best.
Sit with me on the stairs for a while.
Dinner smells good downstairs. I'll watch the door while you eat.
Hum with me, if you want. It keeps the stairs calm.
Evenings are for watching the whole house from here.
Come down before the lights go, won't you?
Who left the lounge window open again?
Has anyone eaten? The kitchen smells fine.
Good work, all of you. Let's keep the house tidy tonight.
Everyone's quiet tonight. I like that.
I'll let the others rest. I'm still awake.
Do you hear that music from the lounge? Lovely.
Tea's on the counter if anyone wants some.
ability: My eyes reach down the hall, farther than most of the house.
A long cone of light runs along the way I'm facing.
Stand inside my beam and I'll know exactly where you are.
My eye light gets brighter once I'm chasing you.
When my eyes turn red, I've already found you.
I'm not guessing. The beam tells me where you stand.
The light in my eyes isn't for show. It's how I see.
Get properly hidden, and my beam will slide right past you.
I can reach you from a long way off, so keep moving.
When I have hold of someone, my eye light goes quiet.
My beam reaches farther than your flashlight does.
Stay off my line, and the beam won't find you.
I'm turning my head. Watch where the beam goes.
Yellow when I'm looking, red once I'm sure.
The beam stops at walls, so the corners are yours.
mechanic: I like the stairs. The third step has the best view.
You dropped your battery. Hold on, I'll wait for you.
That door won't hold me. Think about another way.
No. Not that way. The stairs are behind you.
I don't carry a radar. I just look harder.
The vent is open. Someone's been crawling in there.
Mind the landing. The rug there is slippery.
Careful on the stairs. The rail is loose.
Batteries are heavier than they look, aren't they?
Put the battery back on the shelf, please.
Leave the fuse box alone. The lights need it.
Someone pulled the breaker again. Check the hall.
Don't rattle the vent cover. I can hear that.
A door is open at the top of the stairs.
Pick up what you need, then leave the rest.
Leave the lights alone. I'll notice if you don't.
The relay box is in the hall, by the coats.
Batteries are on the top shelf, if you need one.
The grate on the vent is loose. Mind your fingers.
